Address.description:
A position in a language's namespace: the package it belongs to and the
path within it — `fff :: [grep, types]` for a Rust module, path
components for a TypeScript file. Prefix relations, which are what a move
cares about, never hold across packages.

BatchIntent.description:
Several intents planned in sequence, each against the state the previous
one leaves, and applied as one.

CaptureValue.description: `$A` binds one node; `$$$A` binds a sequence.

name.description: A caller-defined label, such as formatting, compilation, or unit tests.

program.description: Executed directly, without implicit shell parsing.

complete.description: False when capture stopped before EOF or a read failed.

Confidence.description: How sure a rename is that an occurrence refers to its target declaration.

oneOf.description: Declared, imported, or reached by a path that resolves to the target.
A bare token with no evidence either way.
Resolves to a different declaration of the same name.

ContentId.description: Digest of complete file contents, independent of their path.

ContinuationRecovery.description: A recovery action clients can branch on without parsing the error message.

Diff.description:
One file's change: the unified diff text (the wire) and its hunks (the
model).

ErrorCode.description: The kind of failure, stable across releases; the message is not.

oneOf.description: The caller cancelled the operation.
Resolution stopped before a complete answer was available.
The request could not be read: not JSON, or not a known command.
A query with none of pattern, kind, symbol, name.
A pattern or node kind the language's grammar rejects.
A selection naming rows or ids the search did not find.
A template naming a capture the match does not have.
No declaration by that name (and kind).
Several declarations share the name; `declared_in` picks one.
No registered language claims the file.
The language has no layout: paths cannot be followed, files not moved.
A position past the end of the file.
The destination already exists.
A file, or the file declaring a name, could not be found.
The layout refuses the move: a root, across packages, into itself.
Two edits of one plan overlap, or a file is moved twice.
A file changed since the plan (or the apply to undo) was made.
Nothing to undo, or a history file that cannot be read.
Reading or writing the tree failed.
Recovery could not restore or verify every attempted effect.

Failure.description: A failed request, as the wire carries it.

hint.description: What to try instead, when there is something.

recovery.description: Effects that could not be restored after a failed mutation.

FileChange.description: One file a plan touches: its edits and the whole-file diff.

moved_to.description: Path after, when the file is moved.

Intent.description:
Any mutating request, as one value: what history records, what a summary
renders, what a remote client sends.

oneOf.description:
Several intents planned in sequence, each against the state the
previous one leaves, and applied as one.

address.description:
For a declaration in an addressable file: its module address, the
value `outline` gives it. Filled by the engine, which has the project.

content.description: Complete source version; absent only in older serialized matches.

line.description: The source line on which the match starts, for display in context.

MatchId.description:
Content-derived identifier: the same file, range and text yield the same id
across runs, so a selection made from one `search` can drive a later command.

Modifier.description: A visibility modifier as it appears in the source.

MoveIntent.description: Move a file and make every reference to it follow.

MoveSymbolIntent.description:
Move one declaration — with what belongs to it in the text, and for Rust
its `impl` blocks — from the file declaring it to another file of the
same language, and make every reference follow.

to.description: The file to declare it in; it must exist.

Name.description: One identifier: a module, a declaration, a file stem. Compared by text.

Occurrence.description: A token spelling the renamed name, with what the imports could tell.

address.description:
For a declaration in an addressable file: its module address, the
value `outline` gives it. Filled by the engine, which has the project.

content.description: Complete source version; absent only in older serialized matches.

line.description: The source line on which the match starts, for display in context.

PackageId.description:
The name a package goes by in paths: a Rust crate's lib name (`fff`, not
`fff-search`), a TypeScript package's name. The layout decides the spelling.

PlanId.description: Opaque handle scoped to an engine session, not a serializable edit plan.

files.description: Contents written by the transaction. A replay reports this historical result.

history_id.description: Committed history entry, used by the existing history/undo lifecycle.

lifetime_seconds.description: Fixed lifetime from preparation; inspection/retry does not extend it.

validation.description: Latest explicitly requested validation; does not change the apply receipt.

PlanReviewCursor.description: A plan-store cursor. It cannot be used with source-query continue or expand.

PlanReviewItem.description:
Metadata uses the corresponding ordinary preview record shape. Text fields
replaced by empty strings are reconstructed by following JSON-pointer chunks.

Position.description:
Zero-based line and character column. Columns count `char`s, not bytes,
so they are safe to show to humans and editors.

language.description: Restrict to one language; otherwise every registered language is searched.

name.description: Only declarations with exactly this name.

pattern.description: ast-grep style pattern with meta-variables, e.g. `fn $NAME($$$ARGS) { $$$ }`.

Reason.description:
What the file's imports and paths said about an occurrence: the ground
for its [`Confidence`]. Views tag `?` and `✗` sections with it.

oneOf.description: Written in the module that declares the target.
An import resolving to the target brings the name in.
The tail of a qualified path resolving to the target.
A glob (or whole-file) import opens the declaring module.

Reached through a re-export (`use vvv_core::Span` for
`vvv_core::text::span::Span`) that vvv followed to the declaration.

Syntax could not place it; an oracle — a build, a language server —
said it is the declaration.
A bare name nothing imports, or a path whose head cannot be placed.

No declaration to judge against: a method or field, reached through
a type; the token merely spells the name.
Resolves to another declaration of the same name in the workspace.
Resolves into a package outside the workspace.
Syntax could not place it; an oracle said it is another declaration.

Recovery.description: A recovery result; unknown states are separate from confirmed residual effects.

RelPath.description:
A file's path inside the workspace, spelled the way the project does: `/`
on every platform.

A workspace path is a project path — like a `mod` path or a
`crate::a::b` address — not a path of the machine, so it carries its own
spelling and is what goes on the wire, into a row, or into a diagnostic.
It reads as a [`Path`] (an OS path is made from one at the edge, where a
file is actually read), but it cannot spell a separator the host's way:
`Display`, serde and the stored bytes are always `/`.

Rename.description: `vvv rename`: the declaration and every occurrence, each judged.

declarations.description: Where `name` is declared; more than one means the rename is ambiguous.

occurrences.description:
Every identifier spelling the name, each judged against the target;
their ids feed a later `--select`.

RenameIntent.description:
Rename the declaration(s) called `name` and every identifier that spells it.

Resolution is syntactic: every occurrence of the identifier in files of
the declaring language is an occurrence. The `selection` is how a human or
agent excludes the ones that are not the same symbol.

declared_in.description: The file declaring the symbol meant, when several share the name.

Rewrite.description: `vvv rewrite`: one edit per selected match.

RewriteIntent.description: Replace every selected match of `query` with `template`.

Role.description:
What position a match occupies in its file: the declaration itself, a
token inside an import statement, or any other use. Views lead with
declarations and dim imports; the engine orders results by it.

Selection.description:
Which matches of a search a later command acts on.

Ids are content-derived, so a selection made from `vvv search` can be
handed to `vvv rewrite` in a separate process. Ordinals are the 1-based
positions in the same search's result order, which is what human output
numbers rows with. Either kind that no longer resolves means the files
changed in between; the selection is then refused rather than silently
narrowed.

SnapshotId.description: Opaque identity of captured source and project inputs; not a disk transaction.

Span.description: Half-open byte range `[start, end)` inside a single file.

Symbol.description: A declaration found in one file.

extent.description:
The declaration with what belongs to it in the text: leading
attributes and doc comments, an enclosing `export`. What moving the
declaration cuts; what an outline shows.

name_span.description: The identifier token itself: what a rename replaces.

visibility.description:
The visibility as written (`pub(crate)`, `export`); `None` when the
declaration has no modifier. What it means is the language's
[`Semantics`](crate::Semantics).

SymbolKind.description: What a declaration declares, in vocabulary shared by every language.

oneOf.description:
An `impl` block, named after the type it is for. Not a declaration a
path can reach; it travels with its type when the type moves.

passed.description: True only when every command succeeded and observed inputs stayed unchanged.

run.description: Monotonically increasing within this retained plan.

oneOf.description: A failed request, as the wire carries it.

hint.description: What to try instead, when there is something.

recovery.description: Effects that could not be restored after a failed mutation.
